newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT BUT RATES STEADY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY MARKET SHORT BUT RATES STEADY.

text.p: Zimbabwe's money market opened slightly short on Monday but dealers expected liquidity to be restored to the system on maturity of treasury bills, and rates were quoted stable at Friday's levels.
"We had a slight shortage under Saturday's date but that is only temporary because we have a big amount of maturities today," one dealer said.
On Monday, discount houses were taking up treasury bills at 22.49 percent and selling them at 22 percent on the open market, unchanged from Friday.
NCD bills redeemable after 30, 60 and 90 days were also being being bought and sold steadily at 23.5 and 22.5 percent respectively.
Bankers acceptances were trading at 22.65 and 22.25 percent across the board, little changed from 22.75 and 22.25, while call money held on to its previous 22 percent.
Figures from the central Reserve Bank put the market shortage on Monday morning at Z$48 million compared to a previous surplus of Z$876 million.
